words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says prayer is not valid for one who does not obey it, and its obedience restrains indecency and wrong; another transmission leaves the attribution to Ibn Masud.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم -وقال أبو خالد مرة: عن عبد الله -: "لا صلاة لمن لم يطع الصلاة،

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says prayer benefits only the person who obeys it; Ibn Kathir judges this stopped report more sound than the Prophetic attribution.
rows.anchor: قيل لعبد الله: إن فلانا يطيل الصلاة؟ قال: إن الصلاة لا تنفع إلا من أطاعها

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan transmits a Prophetic report that a prayer which fails to restrain indecency only increases its performer’s distance from God.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من صلى صلاة لم تنهه عن الفحشاء والمنكر،

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir judges the stopped reports from Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-A'mash, and others the soundest.
rows.anchor: والأصح في هذا كله الموقوفات عن ابن مسعود، وابن عباس، والحسن وقتادة، والأعمش وغيرهم،

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man reports someone prays but steals in the morning; the Prophet replies that what he says in prayer will restrain him. Al-A'mash initially doubts the chain’s link to Jabir.
rows.anchor: قال رجل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن فلانا يصلي فإذا أصبح سرق، قال: "سينهاه

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: البزار
rows.claim: Al-Bazzar says several transmitters relate this report from al-A'mash but differ over its chain, with routes through Abu Hurayra or another authority, Abu Sufyan from Jabir, and Abu Salih from Jabir.
rows.anchor: وهذا الحديث قد رواه غير واحد عن الأعمش واختلفوا في إسناده

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the question about a man who prays at night and steals by morning; the Prophet says what the man says will restrain him.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إن فلانا يصلي بالليل فإذا أصبح سرق؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer also contains remembrance of God, its greatest intended element; God knows all people’s sayings and deeds.
rows.anchor: وتشتمل الصلاة أيضا على ذكر الله تعالى، وهو المطلوب الأكبر؛

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says prayer has three necessary traits: sincerity commands right, fear restrains wrong, and Quranic remembrance commands and forbids; a prayer without them is not prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية في قوله: {إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر} ، قال: إن الصلاة فيها ثلاث خصال

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: ابن عون الأنصاري
rows.claim: Ibn Awn says a person in prayer is engaged in good and held back from indecency and wrong; the remembrance of God in which he is occupied is greater.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عون الأنصاري: إذا كنت في صلاة فأنت في معروف، وقد حجزتك

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: حماد بن أبي سليمان
rows.claim: Hammad explains that prayer restrains a person from wrong for as long as the person remains in prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال حماد بن أبي سليمان: {إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر} يعني: ما دمت فيها.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God’s remembrance of His servants is greater than their remembrance of Him; Mujahid and others report this interpretation too.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ولذكر الله أكبر} ، يقول: ولذكر الله لعباده أكبر،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report about remembering God at meals and bedtime, Ibn Abbas agrees that God’s remembrance of people is greater than their remembrance of Him, citing 2:152.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {ولذكر الله أكبر} قال: ذكر الله عند طعامك وعند منامك.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas gives two senses: remembering God with regard to what He forbade, and God’s remembrance of you being greater than your remembrance of Him.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ولذكر الله أكبر} قال: لها وجهان،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas rejects prayer’s praises and Quran recitation as the meaning; it means God’s remembrance of people when they remember Him in obeying commands or avoiding prohibitions, which Ibn Jarir selects.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن ربيعة قال: قال لي ابن عباس: هل تدري ما قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This interpretation is transmitted through several routes from Ibn Abbas and also from Ibn Masud, Abu al-Darda, Salman al-Farisi, and others; Ibn Jarir chose it.
rows.anchor: وقد روي هذا من غير وجه عن ابن عباس. وروي أيضا عن ابن مسعود، وأبي الدرداء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God can originate creation, He can restore it; people return to Him on Judgment Day, when He repays each person according to deeds.
rows.anchor: يقول تعالى: {الله يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده} أي: كما هو قادر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the criminals will despair.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ييأس المجرمون.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the criminals will be exposed; another narration says they will grieve.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يفتضح المجرمون. وفي رواية: يكتئب المجرمون.

words: وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُم مِّن شُرَكَآئِهِمْ شُفَعَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deities worshipped apart from God will not intercede; the worshippers disown them, and they betray them when most needed.
rows.anchor: ما شفعت فيهم الآلهة التي كانوا يعبدونها من دون الله، وكفروا بهم وخانوهم أحوج ما كانوا إليهم.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada calls this the final division with no reunion: one group rises to the highest levels and another falls to the lowest.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: هي -والله -الفرقة التي لا اجتماع بعدها، يعني: إذا رفع هذا إلى عليين،

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada explain that the believers will be made blissful.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد وقتادة: ينعمون.

rows.speaker: يحيى بن أبي كثير
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir interprets the believers’ bliss as hearing singing; Ibn Kathir says the word’s sense is broader.
rows.anchor: وقال يحيى بن أبي كثير: يعني سماع الغناء. والحبرة أعم من هذا كله،

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: Al-Ajjaj’s line uses hibr for gratitude and the happiness given to the allies of truth, as poetic evidence for bliss.
rows.anchor: قال العجاج: الحمد (1) لله الذي أعطى الحبر

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada say the heavens have no columns, visible or invisible.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة: ليس لها عمد مرئية ولا غير مرئية.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, and Mujahid instead say the heavens have columns people cannot see.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، وعكرمة، ومجاهد: لها عمد لا ترونها.

words: وَأَلْقَىٰ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ رَوَٰسِىَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains anchor and weigh the earth so it does not shake with its inhabitants over the water.
rows.anchor: يعني: الجبال أرست الأرض وثقلتها لئلا تضطرب بأهلها على وجه الماء؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God scattered every kind of animal on earth; only its Creator knows the number of forms and colors.
rows.anchor: وذرأ فيها من أصناف الحيوانات مما لا يعلم عدد أشكالها وألوانها إلا الذي خلقها

words: فَأَنۢبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍۢ كَرِيمٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every noble pair is a kind of plant that is beautiful in appearance.
rows.anchor: أي: من كل زوج من النبات كريم، أي: حسن المنظر.

words: فَأَنۢبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍۢ كَرِيمٍ
rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi says people too are plants of earth: whoever enters Paradise is noble, while whoever enters Hell is vile.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: والناس -أيضا -من نبات الأرض، فمن دخل الجنة فهو كريم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens, earth, and all between are created and determined by God alone, without partner; worshippers are challenged to show what their idols created.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {هذا خلق الله} أي: هذا الذي ذكره تعالى من خلق السموات، والأرض وما بينهما، صادر عن فعل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are polytheists who worship others beside God; their state is manifest ignorance and blindness.
rows.anchor: يعني: المشركين بالله العابدين معه غيره {في ضلال} أي: جهل وعمى، {مبين} أي: واضح ظاهر لا خفاء به.

words: إِنَّهَآ إِن تَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍۢ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the pronoun most likely refers to an injustice or sin as tiny as a mustard seed; some instead read it as the pronoun of the situation, with mithqal nominative on that reading.
rows.anchor: أي: إن المظلمة أو الخطيئة لو كانت مثقال حبة [من] (5) خردل. وجوز بعضهم أن يكون الضمير في قوله: {إنها} ضمير الشأن والقصة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day God brings the deed forth when the just scales are set and repays good with good and evil with evil.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {يأت بها الله} أي: أحضرها الله يوم القيامة حين يضع الموازين القسط، وجازى عليها إن خيرا فخير،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s subtle knowledge means nothing escapes Him, however tiny; He is aware even of an ant’s movement in deep night.
rows.anchor: أي: لطيف العلم، فلا تخفى عليه الأشياء وإن دقت ولطفت وتضاءلت {خبير} بدبيب النمل في الليل البهيم.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi relates, through a route from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud, and other Companions if sound, that the rock is beneath the seven earths; similar views are attributed to Atiyya, Abu Malik, al-Thawri, and others.
rows.anchor: ذكره السدي بإسناده ذلك المطروق عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وجماعة من الصحابة إن صح ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir considers the under-seven-earths report likely Israelite material, neither affirmed nor denied; the apparent meaning is that God exposes even a speck hidden in solid rock.
rows.anchor: والظاهر -والله أعلم -أن المراد: أن هذه الحبة في حقارتها لو كانت داخل صخرة،

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Said al-Khudri reports the Prophet saying that if someone acted in a solid rock with no opening, his deed would still come out to people.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري، رضي الله عنه، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists acknowledge God alone created the heavens and earth, yet worship partners they admit are His creation and property; their confession establishes proof, though most do not understand.
rows.anchor: إنهم يعرفون أن الله خالق السموات والأرض، وحده لا شريك له، ومع هذا يعبدون معه شركاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God as His creation; He needs nothing, everything needs Him, and He is praised for creation, law, and all affairs.
rows.anchor: أي: هو خلقه وملكه، {إن الله هو الغني الحميد} أي: الغني عما سواه، وكل شيء فقير إليه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s grandeur, sublime names and attributes, and perfect words cannot be encompassed; the Prophet says he cannot enumerate praise as God praises Himself.
rows.anchor: كما قال سيد البشر وخاتم الرسل

words: وَلَوْ أَنَّمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مِن شَجَرَةٍ أَقْلَٰمٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If all trees became pens and the sea, joined by seven more seas, became ink to write of God’s majesty, pens would break and water run out, even with more supplies.
rows.anchor: أي: ولو أن جميع أشجار الأرض جعلت أقلاما، وجعل البحر مدادا ومده سبعة أبحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seven is rhetorical intensification, not a limit or a claim that seven seas surround the world; that literal claim comes from Israelite material neither confirmed nor denied.
rows.anchor: على وجه المبالغة، ولم يرد الحصر ولا [أن] (3) ثم سبعة أبحر موجودة تحيط بالعالم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quran 18:109 similarly says the sea would run out before God’s words; ‘another like it’ means repeated further supplies without limit.
rows.anchor: بل كما قال تعالى في الآية الأخرى: {قل لو كان البحر مدادا لكلمات ربي لنفد البحر

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri says that if trees were pens and seas ink, God’s decrees would exhaust the seas and break the pens.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: لو جعل شجر الأرض أقلاما، وجعل البحر مدادا، وقال الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says polytheists claimed this speech would soon run out; the verse answers that God’s wonders, wisdom, creation, and knowledge would not be exhausted.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: قال المشركون: إنما هذا كلام يوشك أن ينفد، فقال الله تعالى: {ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام}

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas compares all human knowledge with God’s knowledge to a drop of water beside all the seas.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: إن مثل علم العباد كلهم في علم الله كقطرة من ماء البحور كلها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if every tree were a pen and every sea ink, pens and water would run out while God’s words remain; no one can fully measure or praise Him except by His own praise.
rows.anchor: لانكسرت الأقلام، وفني ماء البحر، وبقيت كلمات الله قائمة لا يفنيها شيء؛ لأن أحدا لا يستطيع أن يقدر قدره،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Jewish scholars in Medina asked whether the warning that people received little knowledge referred to them or Muhammad’s people; the Prophet said no, and explained their Torah knowledge was little beside God’s but enough for them. The verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير أو عكرمة، عن ابن عباس؛ أن أحبار يهود قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمدينة: يا محمد، أرأيت قولك:

words: وَلَوْ أَنَّمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مِن شَجَرَةٍ أَقْلَٰمٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports from Ikrima and Ata ibn Yasar also make the occasion Medinan, but the better-known view is that the sura and verse are Meccan; Ibn Kathir says God knows best.
rows.anchor: وهكذا روي عن عكرمة، وعطاء بن يسار. وهذا يقتضي أن هذه الآية مدنية لا مكية، والمشهور أنها مكية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aziz means God has subdued everything, with no one able to prevent His will or overturn His judgment; al-Hakim describes His wisdom in creation, commands, speech, deeds, law, and all affairs.
rows.anchor: أي: عزيز قد عز كل شيء وقهره وغلبه، فلا مانع لما أراد ولا مخالف ولا معقب لحكمه، {حكيم} في خلقه وأمره،

words: مَا خَلْقُكُمْ وَلَا بَعْثُكُمْ إِلَّا كَنَفْسٍ وَٰحِدَةٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating and resurrecting everyone is as easy for God as creating one person; His single command brings a thing into being, as 36:82, 54:50, and 79:13–14 show.
rows.anchor: أي: ما خلق جميع الناس وبعثهم يوم المعاد بالنسبة إلى قدرته إلا كنسبة [خلق] (2) نفس واحدة، الجميع هين عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears their words and sees their deeds just as He hears and sees one person; His power over all is likewise like His power over one.
rows.anchor: كما هو سميع لأقوالهم بصير بأفعالهم كسمعه وبصره بالنسبة إلى نفس واحدة كذلك قدرته عليهم كقدرته على نفس واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Resurrection the polytheists stand humbled before God, heads bowed from shame; they say they now hear His words and obey His command, as in 19:38.
rows.anchor: حين عاينوا البعث، وقاموا بين يدي الله حقيرين ذليلين، ناكسي رؤوسهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask to return to worldly life to do good, now certain of God’s promise and meeting; if returned, they would again disbelieve and disobey, as 6:27–29 says.
rows.anchor: وقد علم الرب تعالى منهم أنه لو أعادهم إلى الدار الدنيا لكانوا كما كانوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their later self-reproach says listening or reasoning would have kept them from the blazing Fire, as 67:10 states.
rows.anchor: لو كنا نسمع أو نعقل ما كنا في أصحاب السعير}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could have given every soul guidance if He willed, just as 10:99 says He could have made everyone on earth believe.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى {ولو شاء ربك لآمن من في الأرض كلهم جميعا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to taste the Fire’s punishment is rebuke and reproach.
rows.anchor: ذوقوا عذاب النار الذي كنتم به تكذبون} أي: يقال لهم ذلك تقريعا وتوبيخا.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and many authorities identify the nearer punishment as worldly calamities, illness, and afflictions meant to lead people to repentance.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: يعني بالعذاب الأدنى مصائب الدنيا وأسقامها وآفاتها، وما يحل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In another narration, Ibn Abbas identifies the nearer punishment as carrying out legal penalties.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس -في رواية عنه -: يعني به إقامة الحدود عليهم.

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب ومجاهد وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Al-Bara ibn Azib, Mujahid, and Abu Ubayda interpret it as punishment in the grave.
rows.anchor: وقال البراء بن عازب، ومجاهد، وأبو عبيدة: يعني به عذاب القبر.

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah says the nearer punishment meant drought years that struck the people; al-Nasa'i records the report without a grading here.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله: {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر} قال: سنون أصابتهم.

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b says the nearer punishment includes calamities and the smoke that had passed, while the great assault and al-lizam remained; Muslim transmits a similar mawquf report, as does al-Bukhari from Ibn Masud.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: In another narration Ibn Masud says the nearer punishment was killing and captivity at Badr; Malik reports likewise from Zayd ibn Aslam.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود (9) أيضا، في رواية عنه: العذاب الأدنى: ما أصابهم من القتل والسبي يوم بدر.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and others say every Meccan household grieved for a dead or captive relative; some faced an affliction or paid ransom, and some both.
rows.anchor: قال السدي وغيره: لم يبق بيت بمكة إلا دخله الحزن على قتيل لهم أو أسير،

words: مَا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِّن قَلْبَيْنِ فِى جَوْفِهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage gives physical examples before its moral point: one person has one heart, a wife under zihar is not a mother, and an adopted person is not a biological son; 58:3 says mothers are those who gave birth.
rows.anchor: كما لا يكون للشخص الواحد قلبان في جوفه، ولا تصير زوجته التي يظاهر منها بقوله: أنت علي كظهر أمي أما له،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adoption rule was revealed about Zayd ibn Haritha, whom the Prophet adopted before prophethood and who was called Zayd ibn Muhammad; 33:40 says Muhammad is not father to any of the men.
rows.anchor: فإنها نزلت في شأن زيد بن حارثة مولى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قد تبناه قبل النبوة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling an adopted person a son does not make him a true son: he comes from another man’s loins and cannot have two fathers, just as one person cannot have two hearts.
rows.anchor: يعني: تبنيكم لهم قول لا يقتضي أن يكون ابنا حقيقيا، فإنه مخلوق من صلب رجل آخر،

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr explains that God speaks the truth in the sense of justice.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير {يقول الحق} أي: العدل.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains that God guides the path by guiding to the straight way.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: {وهو يهدي السبيل} أي: الصراط المستقيم.

words: مَا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِّن قَلْبَيْنِ فِى جَوْفِهِ
rows.speaker: غير واحد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrima, al-Hasan, and Qatada report that the verse concerned a Qurayshi man called Dhu al-Qalbayn, who claimed to have two hearts; Ibn Jarir chose this account.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر غير واحد: أن هذه الآية نزلت في رجل من قريش، كان يقال له:

words: مَا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِّن قَلْبَيْنِ فِى جَوْفِهِ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after the Prophet was briefly distracted in prayer, hypocrites joked he had one heart with them and another elsewhere; the verse was revealed in response. Al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan.
rows.anchor: قلت لابن عباس: أرأيت قول الله تعالى (1) :

words: مَا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِّن قَلْبَيْنِ فِى جَوْفِهِ
rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri says the one-heart example was an analogy for Zayd ibn Haritha: another man’s son is not your son; Mujahid, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd also say the verse was revealed about Zayd.
rows.anchor: عن الزهري، في قوله: {ما جعل الله لرجل من قلبين في جوفه} قال: بلغنا أن ذلك كان في زيد بن حارثة،
